newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: ALP KEEPS UP PRESSURE OVER MINISTERIAL CONFLICTS
The Labor Party is trying to keep the pressure on the Federal Government over the issue of share- ownership and possible ministerial conflicts of interests.
The Prime Minister has defended Industry Minister, John Moore, who's the Opposition's latest target.
The Opposition has questioned Mr Moore's ownership of shares in Bligh Ventures, a company with holdings in the petroleum, technology and telecommunications companies.
Mr Moore has told Parliament he's put his shares up for sale, but only some have been sold so far.
Mr Howard's office says Mr Moore has taken all reasonable steps to divest himself of the shares ...and has also been careful not to place himself in a position of having a conflict of interest.
The office says Mr Howard doesn't expect Ministers to take a massive loss on share sales, although he doesn't believe they should hold out for the best possible price.
KEW COTTAGES INQUESTS
Staff at Melbourne's Kew Cottages took 25 minutes to give firefighters an accurate account of people trapped in blazing units where nine intellectually-disabled people died in April.
As the inquest on the deaths started yesterday, the coroner Graeme Johnston heard fire officers were told three times, nobody remained in the buildings.
He heard two carers were looking after 36 residents on the night of the fire, and installation of a sprinkler system had been stopped when asbestos was found.
The coroner inspected the site, and was urged to look into staffing levels, emergency procedures, and fire safety equipment as well as the cause of the blaze.
The inquest continues today.
DINOSOUR TRACKS STOLEN IN WESTERN AUSTRALIA
Thieves have used power tools to hack a set of 130 million year old dinosaur footprints from a sacred site in the Kimberley region of Western Australia.
The fossils, the only known Stegosaur footprints in the world, are the only evidence that the Stegosaur existed in Australia.
The West Australian Museum's Ken McNamara, says the theft, is devastating for studies of the area, which were still being carried out.

Aboriginal communities near Broome have expressed deep concern over the theft of the fossils which were within the boundaries of a native title claim application lodged by the Goolarabooloo and Jabirjabir peoples.
WA INVESTIGATION OF GOLDFIELDS MP
In Western Australia, Goldfields Labor parliamentarian Julian Grill has questioned the motives behind a prolonged police investigation into his financial affairs.
Mr Grill says he has now been continually investigated for seven years and nothing has been found against him.
Charges were laid and then dropped and since then the Official Corruption Investigation Squad had looked at different matters that have led nowhere.
Mr Grill says he cannot contemplate going back into the shadow cabinet until the police investigations are completed.

Detective Sergeant Trevor Porter, of the Official Corruption Investigation Squad, says the reason their investigations are taking so long is that as they pursue one line of inquiry they find new information that needs further investigation.
MINING UNION DEAL WITH BHP
Australia's top mining union the CFMEU has made a deal with Australia's biggest coal exporter, BHP, to limit industrial action and promote exports.
The just finalised six-year National Framework Agreement covers more than 5,000 coal workers in New South Wales and Queensland.
CFMEU Federal President John Maitland says the agreement, which will be used as a basis for future enterprise agreements, shows the union's commitment to the development of Australian industry.
Mr Maitland says it gives BHP the confidence to be able to significantly increase their investment, and guarantees higher wages and job security for workers.
ATSIC COUNCILLOR SAYS HANSON WAS RECEPTIVE
An Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Commission councillor on Palm Island says Independent MP Pauline Hanson was open to her point of view when they met on Palm Island yesterday.
Ms Hanson spent about two hours on the Island, home to Australia's largest Aborigninal community.
A group of Aboriginal women who waited for three hours to talk to the controversial M-P said that they respected her opinion.
ATSIC councillor Sylia Reuben says despite Ms Hanson's openness yesterday, she'll be fighting against her call for the dumping of ATSIC.
Ms Reuben says instead trying to abolish the organisation, she should set about finding out why its funding isn't getting through to the grass roots levels were it's needed.
SHOOTERS PARTY GEARS UP FOR BY-ELECTION
The Shooters party has targeted immigration and gun control in its campaign launch for Saturday's by-election in the Federal seat of Lindsay.
New South Wales Shooters MP, John Tingle, says race is not an issue but immigration should be reduced when there's high unemployment.
He also says there's too much emphasis on immigration for family reunions.
On the guns issue, Mr Tingle said a Labor win in Lindsay would send the Prime Minister a message that the shooters in the western Sydney electorate are angry at his national gun laws.
Mr Tingle says he believes shooters preferences will give the seat to former ALP Minister Ross Free, with Shooters candidate Rod Franich attracting ten per cent of the vote.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
